proof_summary: Writing the rank as \(n+\lfloor e^{H_n}-1\rfloor\), the proof shows \(1<e^{H_{n+1}}-e^{H_n}<2\) using elementary logarithm/exponential inequalities, monotonicity of \(H_n-\log n\), and explicit estimates for the initial cases; hence the floor increment is 1 or 2 and every rank increment is 2 or 3. Since \(H_n-\log n\to\gamma\), telescoping the increments gives limiting densities \(e^\gamma-1\) and \(2-e^\gamma\), so their ratio tends to \((e^\gamma-1)/(2-e^\gamma)\); finite rational bounds \(16/9<e^\gamma<41/23\) place this limit strictly between 3.5 and 3.6.
